clue.text: Body part problem the drink regularly feeds

indicators.note: the picked letters are fed into the middle of the problem word

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem set in school

indicators.note: taking every other letter of the words the drink, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A medical worry: some part of the body is troubled because of what someone keeps drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks the first, third, fifth and seventh letters, giving a seabird, and 'feeds' puts it inside the problem word.
explanation.definitionFit: The breastbone, a flat bone at the front of the chest, is a part of the body.

clue.text: Get cracking half of shandy with barrelled beer!

indicators.note: half of means the first half of the letters of the word
with here means the beer is held within the barrel word

parts.note: a keg is a small barrel, so the barrelled container supplies the word for it
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: An order to hurry up and drink a half shandy along with some keg beer.
explanation.walkthrough: Shandy is beer mixed with lemonade; 'half of' takes its first three letters. The setter intends 'barrelled' to do double duty, giving the keg and putting the ale inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal commands to hurry up and start moving quickly.

clue.text: Upset about quote to bring in new siren?

indicators.note: the reversed letters bring in the new letter
in a down clue upset turns the letters upwards, so they read backwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning
to cite is to quote

explanation.surface: Someone annoyed about a price quote that brings in a new alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' turns RECITE into ETICER, and N goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A siren in myth lured sailors with song, so is one who tempts or lures.

clue.text: Note balance lacking in Head racket

indicators.note: the balance word is lacking its head, its first letter

parts.note: poise is balance or composure

explanation.surface: A tennis player's racket lacks balance at its head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'racket' looks like the tennis bat, but it means din.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket is a loud din, which is unwanted sound.

clue.text: Cruel way to cut down on politeness in Paris?

indicators.note: on here means the reduced word goes after, following the French word

parts.note: merci, French for thank you, is the polite word a Parisian uses
less means cut down, reduced in amount

explanation.surface: Advice on how to be ruder in France: stop saying thank you so much.
explanation.walkthrough: Merci is French for thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing no pity or compassion to others is the essence of cruelty.

clue.text: A jet payload sending soldiers wheeling to right

indicators.note: the turned soldiers are put at the right-hand end of what remains
sending the soldiers off takes their letters out of the cargo word

parts.note: freight is the cargo or load a vehicle carries
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

indicators.note: wheeling turns the soldiers round so they face the other way

explanation.surface: A military aircraft's cargo is a load of troops being flown off somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: RE leaves FREIGHT (leaving FIGHT), then 'wheeling' turns RE into ER, which goes 'to right', at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A fighter is a jet warplane built for combat with other aircraft.

clue.text: During one, corpulent nurses start to shrink

definitions.text: During one, corpulent nurses start to shrink

indicators.note: nurses means holds or cradles, so the letter sits inside the corpulent word

parts.note: corpulent means fat

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: While going without food, overweight people get smaller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'During one' refers to the answer itself: during a fast, the fat shrink.
explanation.definitionFit: A period of going without food is when the overweight shed pounds.

clue.text: One with pineapple on top of rifle?

definitions.text: One with pineapple on top of rifle?

indicators.note: the one wears the grenade on, so the grenade wraps round it

parts.note: pineapple is old soldiers' slang for a hand grenade
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

explanation.surface: A soldier with a grenade fitted to the end of his rifle.
explanation.walkthrough: The pineapple is a grenade, not fruit. Hoskins reads I 'with GRENADE on', wearing it, giving GRENAD(I)E, then R from 'top of rifle'.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally a soldier armed with grenades, later a member of an elite infantry regiment.

clue.text: Times breaking story on royal gossip

indicators.note: in a down clue the story sits on top of the royal
the times break into the story

parts.note: a tale is a story
T is time, so two Ts are times

explanation.surface: A newspaper story about a royal is just tittle-tattle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper, but it gives TT.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattler is a person who gossips or tells tales.

clue.text: Pass on spliff, having dropped second pill

indicators.note: the second of the pill letters is dropped from the word

parts.note: a reefer is a cannabis cigarette, as is a spliff
E is slang for an ecstasy pill

explanation.surface: Someone declines a joint after taking another tablet.
explanation.walkthrough: Of the two Es in REEFER, the second one goes.
explanation.definitionFit: To refer a matter is to pass it on to someone else to deal with.

clue.text: Emit gas, but not loudly — that's cunning

indicators.note: not loudly means the loud marking is taken away from the word

parts.note: to fart is to break wind
f (forte) is the musical direction for loudly

explanation.surface: A cheeky boast: breaking wind quietly is the clever way to do it.
explanation.definitionFit: Art can mean craft or guile, as in 'the art of deception', a sense of cleverness.

clue.text: Highly value punching backside-gyrating dope about

indicators.note: the valued word punches into the middle of the turned dope word
only the back end of the word for dope spins round, its final pair swapping order

parts.note: dope is slang for information, inside knowledge
to respect someone is to value them highly

explanation.surface: A wild dance scene: someone prized for twerking while high on drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backside-gyrating' swaps only the final two letters of the dope word, giving INOF, and 'punching' drives the valued word into it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a formal preposition meaning concerning or with regard to.

clue.text: In Beccles, I aroused the congregation of a church

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words that follows, across the word breaks

explanation.surface: A churchgoer in the Suffolk town of Beccles stirred up the local parish.
explanation.walkthrough: Beccles is a small market town in Suffolk, England; the answer runs from its second letter into 'aroused'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecclesia is the Greek word for an assembly, used for the body of worshippers forming a church.

clue.text: Jack has trouble punching small men

indicators.note: the trouble word punches its way into the middle of the small men

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
OR (other ranks) means enlisted soldiers rather than officers
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: Someone called Jack gets into a fight with some little fellows.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack (or jack tar) is an old name for a seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack tar is traditional slang for a seaman of the navy.

clue.text: Big floater seen in canal? Turning bow to left

indicators.note: the bow (front letter) of the boat is turned into the left abbreviation

parts.note: a barge is a flat-bottomed boat used on canals

explanation.surface: A large boat on a canal swings its front end round to port.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'bow' of the boat is its first letter, B, replaced by L.
explanation.definitionFit: Large and big are straightforward synonyms describing great size.

clue.text: I explain stuff in detail for former UKIP member?

parts.note: ex means former, as in an ex-wife
UKIP fought to keep the pound sterling, so a member backs the pound

explanation.surface: A one-time UKIP politician holds forth at length.
explanation.walkthrough: UKIP is the UK Independence Party, which opposed Britain joining the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sets out a theory in detail is an expositor of it.

clue.text: Eastern Lorraine hit by a quake an hour back?

indicators.note: an earthquake shakes the letters of Lorraine into a new order

explanation.surface: A news report: the east of the French region Lorraine was struck by an earthquake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eastern' looks like part of the place description but gives only its abbreviation; 'hit by a quake' shuffles the region's name, which follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: An hour back means at some point before now in time, a little while ago.

clue.text: They sort out problems concerning the lot of you

parts.note: re means concerning
the people doing this crossword are its solvers

explanation.surface: A remark aimed at all the readers about problem-fixers.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who settles a difficulty or dispute is a fixer of it.

clue.text: Item of old riding wear Shetland Island reproduced

indicators.note: reproduced means produced again in another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A historic riding garment from the Shetland Islands is copied.
explanation.walkthrough: Shetland is a group of islands north of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A nithsdale is an 18th-century woman's hooded riding cloak.

clue.text: Top old glass up for couple propping up the bar?

indicators.note: up can mean in disorder or upset, so these letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A drinker raises an old glass to someone, perhaps a pair of regulars leaning on the pub counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' rearranges TOP, O and GLASS. The definition is not a pair of drinkers but the two uprights holding a crossbar.
explanation.definitionFit: On a football pitch the two uprights hold up the crossbar, a witty bar-propping pair.

clue.text: No good in yearning for help for a broken heart?

indicators.note: no good means the good letter is left out

parts.note: aspiring means longing or yearning

explanation.surface: A lovelorn person learns that pining does no good.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'broken heart' is not heartbreak but a heart attack.
explanation.definitionFit: This common painkiller is given to heart attack patients to thin the blood.

clue.text: Prove to be mistaken about American behind contracts

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: the word contracts by losing its final letter

parts.note: butt is American slang for the backside

explanation.surface: Someone shows an error in claims about an American's rear end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contracts' trims BUTT to BUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebut is to refute, giving evidence that a claim is false.

clue.text: The Queen's residence in High Barnet?

definitions.meaning: the queen bee lives in her colony's home
barnet is rhyming slang for hair (Barnet Fair), so a tall hairstyle

explanation.surface: A joke that the monarch lives in High Barnet, a district of north London.
explanation.walkthrough: High Barnet is in north London; barnet is Cockney rhyming slang for hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Bees live in a hive, and a towering 1960s hairdo is named after one.

clue.text: A poor excuse to pucker up briefly in bed

indicators.note: the shortened word goes inside the bed word

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

indicators.note: briefly cuts the last letter off the word

parts.note: to pout is to purse or pucker the lips

explanation.surface: Someone turns down a kiss in bed with a lame excuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts POUT to POU, which goes 'in' COT.
explanation.definitionFit: A cop-out is an evasion of responsibility, a feeble excuse for not doing something.

clue.text: Cast a magic spell on church member

parts.note: an arm is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A witch puts a spell on a member of the congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'member' is not a person but a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: To charm can mean to bewitch, to enchant with magic.

clue.text: Drinks can lead to spewing

parts.note: can is slang for prison, as is slammer

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A warning that alcohol can end in vomiting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like a verb, but it is the noun for a prison. Slammers are tequila shots.
explanation.definitionFit: Tequila slammers are mixed shots banged on the bar and downed in one.

clue.text: Saw cats going head to head, one of them Manx

indicators.note: the first cat faces the other way, so the two cats meet at their heads

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

indicators.note: a Manx cat has no tail, so one cat loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone watched two cats fighting, one of them a tailless Manx.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' is not a verb but a saying. Two TOMs head to head make MOT TOM; the second loses its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying, a maxim, like a slogan to live by.

clue.text: Love that can be pricey to purchase?

definitions.meaning: a term of endearment, like darling

explanation.definitionFit: The word serves both as a fond address and as a word for expensive.

clue.text: German bidet put out in a limited edition?

indicators.note: put out suggests disturbed or upset, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A German bathroom fitting is released in a limited run.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortened version of a book is a cut-down, limited edition of it.

clue.text: Woman one would pay to dismiss case

parts.note: I'd is short for I would, one would

indicators.note: the case is the outer letters, which are dismissed

explanation.surface: A woman who would pay money to have a court case dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Ida is a female first name, as in the Gilbert and Sullivan princess.

clue.text: One spreading crap about football team one away from the bottom

parts.note: Man U is short for Manchester United football club

indicators.note: away from means the one letter is taken out of the bottom word

parts.note: the rear is the bottom or backside
a means one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: A rant about a football team one place off the foot of the league.
explanation.walkthrough: Manchester United is an English football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who spreads dung on fields as fertiliser is literally spreading muck.

clue.text: Fancy that yours truly's put on weight

indicators.note: the self word is put on after the weight

parts.note: a stone is a British weight of fourteen pounds
yours truly is a jokey way of saying me, myself

explanation.surface: Someone is surprised to find they have gained weight.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British unit of weight, 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a British exclamation of surprise, just like 'well I never'.
